newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Somague sees rise in profit in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Somague sees rise in profit in 1997.

text.p: Portuguese construction firm Somague has a healthy order book and foresees a 48 percent increase in consolidated net profits year-on-year to 1.371 billion escudos in 1997, company director Artur Gomes said.
At a presentation of the company's activities at the Lisbon bourse, Gomes forecast that Somague's profits would rise to 1.467 billion escudos in 1998 and 1.55 billion in 1999.
Somague had orders for 60 billion escudos, which will "keep the company occupied for more than a year," Gomes said.
Gomes said the company planned to invest 11.2 billion escudos by the end of 1999, including 5.8 billion escudos in construction equipment.
At the end of 1999, net assets of the Somague group were expected to stand at 39.611 billion escudos, compared with 43.442 billion at the end of 1996, he added.
Bank debt was forecast to drop to 7.322 billion escudos in 1999 from 9.841 billion this year.
Somague's vice-president Diogo Vaz Guedes said the company planned to achieve between 20 and 25 percent of its turnover from construction activities abroad by the end of the century.
He did not say what proportion of the company's turnover was presently achieved from operations abroad.
